Chicken Satay Skewers with Peanut Marinade

posted by Sharon Chen on Jul 31, 2026 0 comments »
Jump To Recipe Leave a Review

Chicken satay skewers marinated in a bold peanut, garlic, and ginger sauce, then grilled to smoky perfection. An easy weeknight or party favorite.

Instaread

Few dishes travel as well from street food stalls to backyard grills as chicken satay — it’s simple, craveable, and always a crowd-pleaser. These Chicken Satay Skewers with Peanut Marinade take that classic combination and make it easy enough for a weeknight: juicy chicken thighs soak up a bold marinade of peanut butter, garlic, tamari, sesame oil, and ginger, then hit the grill until golden and charred at the edges.

If you tried my Grilled Tofu Skewers with Peanut Sauce, you already know how well peanut butter works on the grill — here it takes on a different role, soaking into the chicken itself rather than finishing it as a sauce.

No separate dipping sauce required here — the peanut flavor is baked right into the marinade, so every bite is already packed with flavor. A scatter of chopped peanuts, red pepper flakes, and cool cucumber slices finishes things off.

Why This Recipe Works

Chicken thighs are the MVP of this recipe. Unlike chicken breast, thighs stay juicy and tender even with a few extra minutes on the grill, which makes them far more forgiving for skewer cooking. The peanut marinade does double duty — it tenderizes the chicken while it sits, and the natural sugars in the peanut butter help the outside caramelize beautifully once it hits the heat.

Toasted sesame oil and tamari bring depth and saltiness, while fresh ginger and garlic add warmth and brightness that cut through the richness of the peanut butter. It’s a marinade that tastes complex but comes together in one bowl.

StreetSmart Tips for the Best Chicken Satay Skewers

  • Use natural peanut butter. It blends more smoothly into the marinade and clings to the chicken better than the stabilized, sugary kind.
  • Marinate longer if you can. One hour is the minimum, but this chicken gets even better with an overnight soak — the flavor penetrates deeper and the texture turns out more tender.
  • Don’t overcrowd the skewers. Leave a little space between pieces of chicken so heat can circulate and every side gets that golden char.
  • Check for doneness with a thermometer. Chicken thighs are fairly forgiving, but pulling them at exactly 165°F (74°C) internal temperature guarantees juicy results every time.
  • No grill? Bake them. Set a wire rack over a baking sheet, arrange the skewers on top, and bake at 400°F (200°C) for 20 to 25 minutes. The rack keeps the chicken from sitting in its own juices, so you still get nicely browned edges.
  • Storage Tips: Leftover chicken keeps well in the fridge for up to three days. Reheat gently in a skillet to bring back some char, or slice it up and toss it into a rice bowl, noodle salad, or wrap for an easy next-day lunch.

Serving Suggestions

These skewers are satisfying enough to be the main event, but they also play well with others:

  • Over jasmine or coconut rice with extra cucumber on the side
  • Wrapped in lettuce cups with fresh herbs and a squeeze of lime
  • Alongside a crunchy slaw or cucumber salad for a lighter meal
  • As part of a grilling spread with my Ginger Beef Skewers for a mixed-protein cookout

The chopped peanuts and red pepper flakes aren’t just garnish — they add crunch and a little heat that balances the richness of the marinade, so don’t skip them.

Tried these Chicken Satay Skewers? Let me know how they turned out in the comments below — and if you served them with a side or sauce of your own, I’d love to hear about it.

Chicken Satay Skewers with Peanut Marinade

5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star No reviews
  • Author: Sharon Chen
  • Prep Time: 10 minutes
  • Marinating Time: 1 hour
  • Cook Time: 20 minutes
  • Total Time: 1 hour 30 minutes
  • Yield: 8 servings 1x
  • Category: Appetizers, Main Dish
  • Method: Grilling
  • Cuisine: Asian
  • Diet: Dairy-Free, Gluten-Free, Low-Carb
Print Recipe
Pin Recipe

Description

Chicken satay skewers marinated in a bold peanut, garlic, and ginger sauce, then grilled to smoky perfection. An easy weeknight or party favorite.

Ingredients

Scale
  • 3 pounds (1.3 kilograms) chicken thighs, boneless, skinless, cut into 1-inch pieces
  • 2.6 ounces (75 grams) peanuts, chopped, to serve
  • red pepper flakes, to garnish
  • 1 cucumber, peeled & sliced, to garnish

For the Peanut Marinade:

  • 4.5 ounces (130 grams) natural peanut butter, creamy
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons tamari sauce
  • 2 tablespoons sesame oil, toasted
  • 1 tablespoon white wine vinegar
  • 4 green onions, minced, divided
  • 4 tablespoons cilantro, minced
  • 2 teaspoons ground ginger
  • Salt, to taste

Instructions

  1. Make the Peanut Marinade: In a bowl, mix peanut butter, garlic, tamari, sesame oil, white wine vinegar, half the green onions, cilantro, ginger, and salt (optional).
  2. Marinate the Chicken: Add chicken, toss to coat, and marinate for at least 1 hour (or overnight).
  3. Grill the Peanut Chicken Skewers: Preheat a gas grill to 375°F (190°C) to 400°F (200°C) (medium-high heat). Thread marinated chicken onto skewers. Grill the chicken skewers for 10 to 15 minutes, turning every 3 to 4 minutes, until the thickest pieces reach an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C).
  4. Serve: Serve with cucumber slices, chopped peanuts, and red pepper flakes.

Notes

  • These Chicken Satay Skewers can also be made in the oven. When ready to cook, preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Place a wire rack over a baking sheet and lightly grease. Thread marinated chicken onto skewers and bake for 20-25 minutes until cooked through.
